## AudioVisualizer.kt { #audiovisualizer-kt }

The recorded-audio waveform player: a zoomable, seekable view of a recording, as one
self-contained HTML fragment for a box output.

It is *not* a spectrum analyser or a live meter — it shows audio that already exists, with the
interaction an editor expects (wheel to zoom, drag to pan, click to seek, a playhead that tracks
playback) and the browser's own transport underneath.

The one design decision worth knowing: what it draws is a min/max envelope of the *visible*
window, not the whole file decimated. Where a server can summarise a window
(`AudioVisualizerSource.waveformUrl` — Field Audio's waveform endpoint, for instance) the
component asks for one envelope per view, so an hour-long recording costs the same as a bar of
it; where there is no server it decodes the clip in the browser and does the same arithmetic
locally. Either way a single-sample click survives being drawn at 1000 points, which is the whole
point of a min/max envelope over an average.

Start from `Box.displayAudio` for a URL, `Box.displayAudioSamples` for a `FloatArray` you
generated, or `Box.displayAudioBytes` for an encoded clip you have in memory.

## interactionnets.kt { #interactionnets-kt }

Interaction nets as a live-codeable medium: a graph whose nodes rewrite each other wherever two of them
touch principal port to principal port, with a DSL for building nets, a rule language for the rewrites, a
scheduler that decides which collision fires next, and a force-directed layout so you can watch it happen.

Start at `net` to build one, `rules` to say how it rewrites, [`Reducer`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-reducer) to run it, and `Net.toFLines` or
`Box.showInteractionNet` to look at it. [`Lambda`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-lambda) is a ready-made vocabulary (APP, LAM, DUP, ERASE, ROOT,
VAR, CONST) with its own rule book, if you want the classical behaviour rather than your own.

A compact, single-file interaction-net playground meant to be easy to lift into a larger codebase,
but also meant to be a fertile computational substrate for live coding art.

What is in here:
- a small in-memory interaction-net graph model
- a Kotlin DSL for building whole nets and reusable graph fragments
- two rewrite styles:
    1) a declarative "automatic rewiring" DSL built around ext(side, aux)
    2) an escape hatch for arbitrary custom rewrites in ordinary Kotlin
- configurable active-pair scheduling
- a simple force-directed layout with incremental seeding of rewrite RHS nodes at the LHS center
- FLine/output rendering plus SVG export for quick inspection
- a small lambda-oriented bundle including APP, LAM, DUP, ERASE, ROOT, VAR, CONST

Design intent:
- Keep the core tiny and hackable.
- Make the common case pleasant without removing low-level control.
- Be explicit about where the model is still incomplete.
- Treat the system less like a theorem prover and more like a graph chemistry / reactive medium.

The artistic framing:
This file is not most interesting as a route to "real lambda calculus". It is more interesting as a
local, spatial, rewiring-based substrate for live coding. In that framing:

- principal ports are not just logical redex triggers; they are collision points, activation sites,
  rhythmic contact surfaces
- auxiliary ports are not just variables; they can be treated as tension channels, color buses,
  growth directions, continuation hooks, memory strands, or signal paths
- rewrite rules are not merely reductions; they are local laws of motion, branching, fusion,
  mutation, decay, reflection, gating, or pulse propagation
- active-pair scheduling is not merely evaluation order; it is rhythm, phrasing, emphasis, groove,
  cascade control
- layout is not merely display; it is motion memory and can become part of the meaning of the system

DUP and ERASE in this context:
DUP and ERASE are useful here less as strict lambda-calculus machinery and more as artistic growth and
decay primitives.

- DUP can mean branching, echo, motif propagation, splitting a line of force into two descendants,
  or generating two related but diverging futures
- ERASE can mean fade, pruning, absorption, dissipation, culling, or a sink that removes pressure from
  a local region

In a more expressive live system, DUP does not need to be perfectly literal duplication. It can create
two descendants with slight positional offsets, inherited state, hue drift, phase drift, timing skew,
energy split, or generation markers. Likewise ERASE does not need to be instantaneous deletion; it can
become gradual attenuation, shrinkage, or multi-frame disappearance.

Why this is promising for live coding art:
- Local causality: every visible change comes from a small neighborhood interaction.
- Spatial meaning: the graph is data and choreography at once.
- Compositionality: a small table of rewrite laws can yield rich large-scale behavior.
- Performability: rules, scheduler, layout constants, render mapping, and node injection can all be
  changed while the system is running.

Activation order as an instrument:
Reduction order is a first-class artistic control. A deterministic scheduler can feel mechanical;
randomized scheduling can shimmer; energy-biased or cursor-biased scheduling can create bursts,
avalanches, attraction, or spotlighting. Treat scheduling as part of the score.

Layout as part of computation:
The incremental layout already gives new RHS nodes a positional memory by seeding them at the centroid
of the consumed active pair before relaxation. That idea can be pushed further. Rewrite rules can read
or influence geometry; branch direction can depend on current edge angle; replication distance can
depend on energy; eligibility can depend on local spatial conditions; layout velocity can feed rendering
or sound. The graph need not be computed first and visualized second.

A "wet" semantics is often better than a perfectly dry one:
For artistic purposes, clean instantaneous replacement is sometimes less interesting than sticky,
physicalized replacement. Newly created nodes can inherit centroid and velocity. Consumed edges can
leave ghosts. Erased nodes can decay over a few frames. Duplicated nodes can repel strongly at birth
and then settle. Rules can emit transient sparks or decorative residues. These choices improve visual
legibility and expressiveness during rapid change.

The next high-leverage extension is per-node state:
Adding a small mutable state record to each node would make the substrate much richer. Examples:

    data class State(
        var energy: Double = 1.0,
        var phase: Double = 0.0,
        var hue: Double = 0.0,
        var age: Double = 0.0
    )

Then rewrite rules can split energy on DUP, accumulate age, drift hue, mutate phase, and directly map
these quantities to radius, stroke weight, opacity, curvature, synthesis parameters, or triggering.

Rendering and sound hooks:
A rewrite can be more than a topology update. In a live system it is natural for a rewrite to also emit
events such as "flash this edge", "trigger a note", "spawn a particle", "increase camera pull", or
"mark this component active". That turns graph rewriting into the event engine for an audiovisual system.

Useful node archetypes for an artistic palette:
- Pulse   : propagates motion or activation
- DUP     : bifurcates structure or motive
- ERASE   : consumes / attenuates / prunes
- Delay   : holds activity for N frames or beats
- Gate    : conditionally passes or blocks interaction
- Mirror  : swaps neighborhoods / reflects flow
- Fuse    : merges strands
- Noise   : injects stochastic variation
- Anchor  : spatial stabilizer
- Bloom   : expands into decorative local structure

A note on rigor:
This file adds DUP and ERASE agents in the usual explicit-resource spirit, but it is not trying to be a
complete optimal reducer. There is no full fan/fan commuting story, no full lambda frontend, and no
claim of theoretical completeness. That is deliberate. The value here is as a hackable medium with:

- topology that changes
- space that remembers
- order that matters
- small laws that create style

In other words: treat this as a graph chemistry for live coding.

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">writeSvg</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">path</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">900</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">700</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Writes the net as an SVG file at `path` — `Net.toSvg` straight to disk, on white. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">showInteractionNet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">channel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;interaction-net&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">summaryChannel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;$channel-summary&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;Interaction net&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">w</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">920.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">h</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">560.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">fitToSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Draws the net into this box's output and puts its summary card beside it — the one call a live sketch needs per frame. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">showInteractionSummary</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">channel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;interaction-net-summary&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">vararg</span> <span class="n">cards</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Displays several HTML cards side by side in one responsive grid in this box's output. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">Box</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">showInteractionOverview</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">graphicLines</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">cards</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">channel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;interaction-net-overview&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">graphicTitle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;Comparison&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">graphicWidth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1040.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">graphicHeight</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">340.0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Displays a row of summary cards with one shared drawing underneath, as a single HTML block, and returns that HTML. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">interactionSummaryGrid</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">vararg</span> <span class="n">cards</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Wraps HTML cards in a responsive grid — columns of at least 260px, as many as fit — and returns the markup. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">ReductionStep</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">summaryHtml</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;Reduction step&quot;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | An HTML card describing one reaction: the rule that fired, whether the pair was matched swapped, which node ids went and which arrived, and every event emitted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | A worked example of the whole pipeline, as a runnable `main`: build each [`Lambda`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-lambda) demo net, relax it, reduce it and write before/after SVGs. |

### LayoutConfig { #interactionnets-kt-layoutconfig }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LayoutConfig</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">repulsion</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2500.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">springLength</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">90.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">springStrength</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.015</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">damping</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.82</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timeStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jitter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">8.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clampStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">20.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The knobs on the force-directed layout that `Net.relax` runs — every node pushing every other apart, every edge pulling its two ends together.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">repulsion</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | How hard every node pushes every other away. Falls off as `1/d²`, so it sets the empty space between unconnected nodes without much affecting connected ones. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">springLength</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | The distance an edge is happy at, in position units. The quickest single knob for the overall scale of the picture. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">springStrength</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | How strongly an edge pulls back toward `springLength`. Large values make the net rigid and jittery. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">damping</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Velocity retained per step. Below 1 is what makes the simulation settle at all; toward 1 it wobbles for far longer, and at 1 it never stops. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timeStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Integration step. Scales both the velocity update and the movement, so raising it is a faster but less stable simulation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">jitter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Stored but **unused** by the current layout step — new nodes get their initial scatter from `Net.create` instead. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clampStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Per-step speed limit, in position units. What stops two nearly coincident nodes from firing each other off the canvas. |

### NodeState { #interactionnets-kt-nodestate }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">NodeState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">energy</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">phase</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">hue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">age</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">scalars</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">linkedMapOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The mutable per-node payload that turns a bare interaction net into something worth watching: four named quantities the renderer already reads, plus `scalars` for anything else you want to carry.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">energy</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Drives node radius when drawn, and is what the energy-biased [`PairSelectors`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-pairselectors) rank pairs by. Every operation here floors it at 0, but nothing caps it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">phase</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Carried and split, but **nothing in this file interprets it** — yours to use, though the renderer does fall back to it for a node's port angle when the node has no connected neighbours. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">hue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Drives colour, as a fraction of a turn. Wrapped at render time rather than here, so it may drift far outside `0..1` and that is fine. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">age</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Advanced only by `Net.incrementAges`, in whatever unit you pass it — so age runs on the clock you choose. Nudges drawn lightness. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">scalars</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Room for your own named quantities. Deep-copied by `copyDeep` and blended key-wise by `blend`, where a key missing from one side counts as 0. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">copyDeep</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | An independent copy, `scalars` map included, so later mutation of either cannot reach the other. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">evolved</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">energyScale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">energyBias</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">phaseShift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">hueShift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ageDelta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | A copy with the four quantities moved on — the "one node becomes one node, a little different" step for a rewrite rule to hand its replacement. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">split</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">parts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">branch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">attenuation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">hueSpread</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">phaseSpread</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ageDelta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | One branch's share of this state when a node divides into `parts` — the state side of a DUP-style rewrite. |

### PortKind { #interactionnets-kt-portkind }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">PortKind</span></code>

Which of a node's two kinds of port this is — and therefore whether an edge through it can *react*.

Constants: `PRINCIPAL`, `AUXILIARY`.

### AgentType { #interactionnets-kt-agenttype }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AgentType</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">auxPorts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A kind of node: a name to match rules against, and how many auxiliary ports its instances get.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">arity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Total port count: the auxiliaries plus the one principal port. |

### Port { #interactionnets-kt-port }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Port</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">index</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortKind</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One port on one node — the thing edges connect. Port 0 is always the principal port and `1..auxPorts` the auxiliaries, which is why `Node.aux` takes a 0-based index and adds one for you.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span></code> | The node this port belongs to. A port never moves between nodes. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">index</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Position in the node's `ports` list: 0 is the principal port, `1..auxPorts` the auxiliaries. Note this is the raw index, one more than the number `Node.aux` takes. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortKind</span></code> | Whether this is the one reactive port or an inert auxiliary. Fixed when the node is created. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | `"<nodeId>:<portIndex>"` — the stable string identity [`Net`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-net) uses for its adjacency index. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toString</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The port's `id`. |

### Node { #interactionnets-kt-node }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Node</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One node in a net: an [`AgentType`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-agenttype), a stable `id`, a fixed list of `ports` and a mutable [`NodeState`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-nodestate).

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Unique within its net and never reused, so a [`ReductionStep`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-reductionstep)'s removed ids stay unambiguous after the fact. Minted as `type_n` by [`IdSource`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-idsource) unless you named it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span></code> | Which kind of agent this is — what rules match on, and what fixes the port count. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | This node's mutable payload. `Net.create` copies whatever you pass, so two nodes never share one by accident; a rewrite rule must copy it deliberately. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ports</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | All of this node's ports, principal first at index 0, then the auxiliaries in order. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">principal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span></code> | This node's one reactive port. Wire two of these together and you have an [`ActivePair`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-activepair). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">aux</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span></code> | Auxiliary port `i`, numbered from **0** — so `aux(0)` is `ports[1]`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toString</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | `"<id>:<typeName>"`, e.g. `"dup_4:DUP"`. |

### Edge { #interactionnets-kt-edge }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Edge</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">a</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

An undirected wire between two ports. A port holds at most one edge, so this is a matching, not a graph with multiplicity.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">other</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span></code> | The port at the far end from `p` — how you walk from a node to its neighbour. |

### ActivePair { #interactionnets-kt-activepair }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ActivePair</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">left</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">right</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

Two nodes whose principal ports are wired to each other — a redex, the only place a rewrite can happen.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">canonicalKey</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Pair</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The two node ids sorted, so the same pair always keys the same way whichever side it arrived on. |

### Net { #interactionnets-kt-net }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Net</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ids</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IdSource</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">IdSource</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The net itself: nodes, the wires between their ports, and — because this is meant to be watched — a position and velocity per node.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Collection</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every node, in creation order. A **live view** of the net's own map — do not iterate it while rewriting. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">edges</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Collection</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Edge</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every wire, in creation order. A live view, so a rewrite mid-iteration will upset it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">node</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span></code> | The node with this id. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">positionOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | Where the node currently sits. `(0, 0)` for a node this net has never seen, rather than an exception. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">velocityOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | The node's current layout velocity — `(0, 0)` if it has none yet. Carried across rewrites where a rule asks. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">setPosition</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">p</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Places the node. Stores the vector **by reference**, so mutating the [`Vec2`](math.md#linalg-kt-vec2) you passed moves the node afterwards — pass `Vec2(p)` if that would surprise you. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">setVelocity</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">velocity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Sets the node's layout velocity, copying the vector. A kick here survives into the next `relax`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">create</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">ids</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">next</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">type</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">lowercase</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span></code> | Adds a node of `type` to the net and returns it, with no wires attached. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">remove</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Deletes the node, disconnecting every wire it had first, and forgets its position and velocity. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">connected</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">port</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The port on the other end of this port's wire, or null if it is free. The one-step graph walk. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">connect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Wires two ports together. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">disconnect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Removes the wire between two ports, leaving both free. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">activePairs</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">ActivePair</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every place the net can currently react: each edge joining two principal ports, de-duplicated by `ActivePair.canonicalKey`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">incrementAges</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">dt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Adds `dt` to every node's `age`. Nothing calls this for you, so age advances only on the clock you choose — per frame, per reduction step, per beat. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">relax</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">iterations</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">config</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">LayoutConfig</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">LayoutConfig</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Runs the force-directed layout for `iterations` steps, moving every node. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">totalEnergy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | The sum of every node's `energy` — a one-number read on the whole net. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">averageAge</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Mean node `age`, or 0.0 for an empty net. Rises as the net persists, falls as rewrites replace old nodes with new. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toFLines</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">velocityScale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">18.0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Draws the net: one `FLine` per edge, and several per node — a filled disc and a stroked ring sized and coloured from its [`NodeState`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-nodestate), a spoke per port, a point per port, a halo when the node is half of an active pair, and a streak when it is moving. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">summaryHtml</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s">&quot;Interaction net&quot;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">maxNodes</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A dark-themed HTML card summarising the net — counts, total energy, the highest-energy nodes and the active pairs waiting to fire — for putting in a box output next to the drawing. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toSvg</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">900</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">700</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">padding</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">40.0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The net as a standalone SVG document, on **white** rather than the dark palette the box output uses — the export for putting a net in a paper or a slide. |

### NodeRef { #interactionnets-kt-noderef }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A *name* for a node inside a fragment or a rewrite's right-hand side, standing in for a node that does not exist yet.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toString</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The ref's name, as given. |

### PortRef { #interactionnets-kt-portref }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PortRef</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">node</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">portIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A port on a not-yet-created node: a [`NodeRef`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-noderef) plus a **raw** port index, where 0 is the principal port and the auxiliaries start at 1.

### NetFragment { #interactionnets-kt-netfragment }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">NetFragment</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodeSpecs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">LinkedHashMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">NodeSpec</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">LinkedHashMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pendingInternalConnections</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Pair</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">mutableListOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">publishedPorts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">LinkedHashMap</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">LinkedHashMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A reusable piece of net — some nodes, the wires between them, and a set of named ports it offers to the outside — that can be stamped into a [`Net`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-net) as many times as you like.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">export</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Publishes a port under a name, so whoever embeds this fragment can wire to it without knowing what is inside. |

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FragmentBuilder</span></code>

The receiver inside a `fragment` block: declare nodes, wire them with `to`, and `expose` the ports that should be visible from outside.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">node</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">impulse</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span></code> | Declares a node in the fragment and returns the [`NodeRef`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-noderef) you wire with. Nothing is created yet. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">principal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span></code> | The reactive port of a declared node — the one that can form an active pair. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">aux</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">i</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span></code> | Auxiliary port `i` of a declared node, numbered from **0**. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `principal(a) to aux(b, 0)` — records a wire between two ports of this fragment. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">expose</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">port</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Publishes a port under a name for whoever embeds this fragment. A repeated name replaces the earlier one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">build</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NetFragment</span></code> | The finished [`NetFragment`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-netfragment). `fragment` calls this for you. |

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FragmentEmbed</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodeMap</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>
