### SignatureBinding { #interactionnets-kt-signaturebinding }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">SignatureBinding</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">first</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">second</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">swapped</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A successful [`PairSignature`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-pairsignature) match: the two nodes in the signature's own order, plus whether that meant swapping them relative to how the edge was found.

### RuleMatch { #interactionnets-kt-rulematch }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RuleMatch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rule</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RewriteRule</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">binding</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">SignatureBinding</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

A rule and the binding it matched with — what `RuleBook.findMatch` returns, and what the scheduler chooses between.

### PairContext { #interactionnets-kt-paircontext }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PairContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">first</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">second</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstAuxPeers</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">secondAuxPeers</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">center</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">radius</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstVelocity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">secondVelocity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">axis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

Everything a rewrite rule gets told about the collision it is replacing: the two nodes in signature order, what their auxiliary ports were attached to, and the local geometry.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">first</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span></code> | The node matching the rule signature's *left* type — ordinal 0 throughout the rule DSL, whichever way the edge happened to be stored. About to be deleted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">second</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span></code> | The node matching the signature's *right* type — ordinal 1. Also about to be deleted. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstAuxPeers</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | What each of `first`'s auxiliary ports was wired to, in aux order; a null entry means that port was already free. These are the loose ends the rule must account for. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">secondAuxPeers</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The same for `second`'s auxiliary ports. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">center</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | Midpoint of the two nodes, and the point replacement nodes are seeded at — which is why a rewrite appears to grow out of the collision rather than at the origin. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">radius</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Roughly half the pair's separation, **floored at 12.0** so a coincident pair still gives replacements somewhere to go. The default scale for `branchImpulse`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstVelocity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | `first`'s layout velocity at the moment of the collision, so a replacement can inherit its motion. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">secondVelocity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | `second`'s layout velocity at the moment of the collision. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">axis</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | Unit vector from `first` toward `second`. Falls back to `(1, 0)` for a coincident pair rather than being NaN. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">normal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | Unit vector perpendicular to `axis`. The direction `branchImpulse` throws branches along. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">auxPeer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">auxIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | What auxiliary port `auxIndex` of node `nodeOrdinal` (0 = `first`, 1 = `second`) was wired to — the loose end a rule has to reattach. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">state</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | The **live** state of one of the two nodes — mutating it mutates the doomed node, which is almost never what you want. Use `stateCopy` to seed a replacement. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">stateCopy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | An independent copy of one node's state, safe to hand to a new node and then alter. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">velocity</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | A copy of one node's layout velocity, so a replacement can inherit its motion rather than appearing at rest. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">blendedState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">weightToFirst</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.5</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span></code> | The two states averaged — the state for a rewrite that fuses the pair into one node. See `NodeState.blend`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pairEnergy</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | The pair's combined energy. What the energy-biased [`PairSelectors`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-pairselectors) rank by, and the default event magnitude. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">branchImpulse</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">branch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">branches</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">amount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">radius</span> <span class="o">&#42;</span> <span class="mf">0.35</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | A sideways kick for branch `branch` of `branches`, so replacement nodes fly apart out of the collision instead of being born on top of each other. |

### RewriteEvent { #interactionnets-kt-rewriteevent }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RewriteEvent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">magnitude</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">data</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

Something a rewrite wants the outside world to notice — "flash here", "trigger a note", "spawn a particle" — with a free-text `kind`, a place, a strength and any extra numbers.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Free text naming what happened — `"beta"`, `"spark"`, `"note"`. **Nothing in this file interprets it**, so the vocabulary is entirely yours. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span></code> | Where in layout space it happened. Defaults to the collision centre when emitted from a rule. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">magnitude</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | How much of it there was. Defaults to the pair's combined energy, which makes a decaying rule emit progressively weaker events for free. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">data</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Any extra named numbers the rule wanted to pass along. Copied on emit, so the map you passed is not retained. |

### ReductionStep { #interactionnets-kt-reductionstep }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ReductionStep</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ruleName</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">swapped</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">removedNodeIds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdNodeIds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">events</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">RewriteEvent</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The record of one rewrite that happened: which rule fired, on what, what it removed, what it created and what it emitted.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ruleName</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The `RewriteRule.name` that fired — which is why it is worth naming rules something you would read in a log. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairContext</span></code> | The collision as the rule saw it, including the geometry, so a caller can flash the right place on screen. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">swapped</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether the pair had to be exchanged to match the rule's signature order. Informational; the rule's behaviour does not depend on it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">removedNodeIds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The two consumed nodes' ids. Ids rather than nodes because those nodes are already gone by the time you read this. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createdNodeIds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The ids of the replacement nodes, in the order the rule declared them. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">events</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">RewriteEvent</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Everything the rule emitted, snapshot-copied — so this survives even though the nodes behind it do not. |

### RewriteBuilder { #interactionnets-kt-rewritebuilder }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">RewriteBuilder</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ctx</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The receiver inside a `rule { }` body: declare the nodes that replace the active pair, wire them, and say what happens to the loose ends.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">node</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">impulse</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span></code> | Declares a replacement node and returns its [`NodeRef`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-noderef). Nothing is created until the rule is applied. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">principal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span></code> | The principal port of a replacement node — wire two of these together and the new net can react again. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">aux</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">i</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span></code> | Auxiliary port `i` of a replacement node, numbered from **0**. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | `principal(a) to aux(b, 0)` — wires two ports **inside** the replacement. Applied when the rule fires. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">reconnect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">newPort</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">oldPeer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Attaches a replacement node's port to one of the loose ends the deleted pair left behind — this is how the surrounding net stays connected. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">reconnect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">newPort</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">auxIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | The same as the other `reconnect`, naming the loose end by which node of the pair it belonged to (0 = first, 1 = second) and which of its auxiliary ports — the shorter form, and the one that matches `ext(...)` in the automatic DSL. Silently does nothing if that port was free. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">passthrough</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Wires two of the pair's loose ends **directly to each other**, bypassing the deleted nodes entirely — how you write an ERASE or a plain "these two were connected through me, now connect them" rule. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">emit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">magnitude</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">ctx</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pairEnergy</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">ctx</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">center</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">data</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Records a [`RewriteEvent`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-rewriteevent) for whoever is watching the reduction — a flash, a note, a particle. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">build</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RewriteResult</span></code> | The assembled [`RewriteResult`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-rewriteresult). `RuleBook.rule` calls this for you. |

### RewriteResult { #interactionnets-kt-rewriteresult }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">RewriteResult</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">fragment</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NetFragment</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">NetFragment</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">reconnections</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Pair</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">mutableListOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">passthroughs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Pair</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Port</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">mutableListOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">events</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MutableList</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">RewriteEvent</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">mutableListOf</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

What a rule body produces: the replacement subgraph, how it attaches to the loose ends, which loose ends were joined to each other, and any events emitted.

### RewriteRule { #interactionnets-kt-rewriterule }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RewriteRule</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">signature</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairSignature</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rewrite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">RewriteResult</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One law of motion: a name, the pair of types it fires on, and a function from the collision to its replacement.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | What this law is called. Appears in every [`ReductionStep`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-reductionstep) it produces, so make it readable. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">signature</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairSignature</span></code> | The pair of agent types this fires on, matched in either order. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rewrite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">RewriteResult</span></code> | Called afresh on **every** firing with that collision's context, so the replacement can depend on energy, geometry and velocity rather than being a fixed template. |

### AutoEndpoint { #interactionnets-kt-autoendpoint }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">AutoEndpoint</span></code>

One end of a wire in the automatic-rewiring DSL: either a port of a node the rule is creating ([`InternalEndpoint`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-internalendpoint)) or one of the loose ends the deleted pair left behind ([`ExternalEndpoint`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-externalendpoint)).

### InternalEndpoint { #interactionnets-kt-internalendpoint }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">InternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PortRef</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoEndpoint</span></code>

A port of a node this rule is creating. Produced by `principal(...)` / `aux(...)` in an [`AutoRuleBuilder`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-autorulebuilder).

### ExternalEndpoint { #interactionnets-kt-externalendpoint }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ExternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">auxIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoEndpoint</span></code>

A loose end of the *old* pair: auxiliary port `auxIndex` of pair node `nodeOrdinal` (0 = first, 1 = second).

### AutoRuleBuilder { #interactionnets-kt-autorulebuilder }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">AutoRuleBuilder</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">ctx</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The receiver inside an `autoRule { }` body: declare the replacement nodes and then just say what connects to what, mixing new ports and the old pair's loose ends freely.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">node</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">state</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">NodeState</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">impulse</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span></code> | Declares a replacement node and returns its [`NodeRef`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-noderef). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">principal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">InternalEndpoint</span></code> | The principal port of a node this rule creates, as an endpoint you can wire with `to`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">aux</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ref</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">NodeRef</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">i</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">InternalEndpoint</span></code> | Auxiliary port `i` (from **0**) of a node this rule creates, as a wireable endpoint. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">ext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">nodeOrdinal</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">auxIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ExternalEndpoint</span></code> | One of the **old** pair's loose ends: auxiliary port `auxIndex` of pair node `nodeOrdinal` (0 = first, 1 = second). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">InternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">InternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Wires two ports of the replacement together. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">InternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ExternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Hands one of the old pair's loose ends to a port of the replacement. Ignored if that port was free. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">ExternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">InternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Hands one of the old pair's loose ends to a port of the replacement, written the other way round. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nc">ExternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">other</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ExternalEndpoint</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Splices two of the old pair's loose ends directly to each other — an erase or short-circuit rule. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">emit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">magnitude</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">ctx</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pairEnergy</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">at</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">ctx</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">center</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">data</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Map</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">emptyMap</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Records a [`RewriteEvent`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-rewriteevent) — at the collision centre and with the pair's energy, unless you say otherwise. Same as `RewriteBuilder.emit`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">build</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RewriteResult</span></code> | Resolves every declared connection into the [`RewriteResult`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-rewriteresult) the reducer applies: internal wires stay internal, anything touching an `ext` becomes a reconnection, and two `ext`s become a passthrough. |

### RuleBook { #interactionnets-kt-rulebook }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">RuleBook</span></code>

The table of rewrite laws a net runs under — declare rules into it with `rule` and `autoRule`, and it answers "does anything apply to these two nodes".

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">rule</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">left</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">right</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">rewrite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RewriteBuilder</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Declares a rule with the full-control [`RewriteBuilder`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-rewritebuilder) body — you say what nodes appear and explicitly reconnect or pass through each of the old pair's loose ends. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">autoRule</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">left</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">right</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">rewrite</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoRuleBuilder</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span></code> | Declares a rule with the declarative [`AutoRuleBuilder`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-autorulebuilder) body — you list the connections and the builder works out which are internal, which reattach the old pair's loose ends and which splice two of them together. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">find</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RewriteRule</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The first rule that fires on these two nodes, or null. `findMatch` when you also need the orientation. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">findMatch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">a</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">b</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RuleMatch</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The first rule matching these two nodes, together with the binding that puts them in the rule's own order. |

### ActivationOrder { #interactionnets-kt-activationorder }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">ActivationOrder</span></code>

The ready-made choices for *which* of several possible reactions fires next — reduction order as a dial.

Constants: `FIRST_FOUND`, `LEFTMOST_BY_ID`, `RIGHTMOST_BY_ID`, `RANDOM`, `HIGHEST_PAIR_ENERGY`, `LOWEST_PAIR_ENERGY`.

### PairCandidate { #interactionnets-kt-paircandidate }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PairCandidate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">pair</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ActivePair</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">match</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RuleMatch</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">context</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairContext</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One reaction that *could* happen this step: the active pair, the rule that matched it, and the fully built [`PairContext`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-paircontext) the rule would be given.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rule</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RewriteRule</span></code> | The rule that would fire. Shorthand for `match.rule`. |

### PairSelector { #interactionnets-kt-pairselector }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">PairSelector</span></code>

The scheduler: given every reaction that could fire, pick one — or return null to stop the reduction.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">select</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">candidates</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">PairCandidate</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairCandidate</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Choose the reaction to fire, or null to stop. |

### PairSelectors { #interactionnets-kt-pairselectors }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">PairSelectors</span></code>

The stock [`PairSelector`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-pairselector)s — the schedulers [`ActivationOrder`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-activationorder) names, plus two that it does not.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstFound</span></code> | Takes whichever candidate came first out of the edge set. Cheapest, and the most mechanical-looking. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">leftmostById</span></code> | Prefers the pair containing the alphabetically smallest node id — deterministic, and roughly oldest-first, since ids are minted in creation order. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rightmostById</span></code> | Prefers the pair containing the alphabetically largest node id — deterministic, and roughly newest-first. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">highestPairEnergy</span></code> | Always fires the hottest pair. Tends to produce avalanches and to keep activity concentrated in one region. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lowestPairEnergy</span></code> | Always fires the coldest pair. Tends to spread activity out and to clear up dregs before hot spots. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">random</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">random</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Random</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Random</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Default</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairSelector</span></code> | Fires a uniformly random candidate — the shimmering, non-repeating schedule. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">nearest</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">point</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec2</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairSelector</span></code> | Fires whichever reaction is closest to `point` — activity follows the cursor, or a moving attractor. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">from</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">order</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ActivationOrder</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairSelector</span></code> | The selector for an [`ActivationOrder`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-activationorder). `RANDOM` yields an unseeded `random`, so it is not reproducible. |

### Reducer { #interactionnets-kt-reducer }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Reducer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rules</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RuleBook</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">selector</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PairSelector</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">PairSelectors</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">firstFound</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">layout</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">LayoutConfig</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">LayoutConfig</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The engine: takes a [`RuleBook`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-rulebook) and a scheduler, and runs a net forward one reaction at a time.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">step</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Fires one reaction. False means nothing fired — the net is in normal form, or no rule covers what is left. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">stepDetailed</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ReductionStep</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Fires one reaction and reports what happened, or null if nothing could fire. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">reduce</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">maxSteps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">MAX&#95;VALUE</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">onStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Reduces until nothing can fire or `maxSteps` have run, returning how many fired. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">reduceDetailed</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">net</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">maxSteps</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">MAX&#95;VALUE</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">onStep</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">Net</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">ReductionStep</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | `reduce`, but `onStep` also receives the [`ReductionStep`](visualization.md#interactionnets-kt-reductionstep) — so you can collect the events a whole run emitted rather than just watching the net change. |

### IdSource { #interactionnets-kt-idsource }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">IdSource</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">counter</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The counter behind every automatic node id: hands out `prefix_0`, `prefix_1`, … from **one shared counter**, so ids are unique across prefixes and their numeric order is global creation order.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">next</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">prefix</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The next id: `"${prefix}_$n"`, advancing the shared counter. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">peekCounter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | The counter's current value without consuming it — how many ids have been handed out. Useful for logging. |

### Types { #interactionnets-kt-types }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Types</span></code>

Where agent types come from. A one-function namespace, so `Types.agent("PULSE", 2)` reads as a declaration.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">agent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">auxPorts</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AgentType</span></code> | Declares an agent type with `auxPorts` auxiliary ports — plus the principal port every node has, so its arity is one more than this. |

### Lambda { #interactionnets-kt-lambda }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Lambda</span></code>

This bundle is intentionally pragmatic rather than dogmatic.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">APP</span></code> | Application. Its **principal** port is where the function arrives — that is what meets a `LAM` to beta-reduce — `aux(1)` is the argument, and `aux(0)` is where the result comes back out (the beta rule wires the lambda's body to it). |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">LAM</span></code> | Abstraction. `aux(0)` is the binder (where the argument arrives), `aux(1)` the body. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">DUP</span></code> | Explicit duplication. `aux(0)` and `aux(1)` are the two copies; artistically, a branch or an echo. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">ERASE</span></code> | Explicit deletion — a nullary sink. Artistically, a fade or a drain rather than an instant delete. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">VAR</span></code> | A free variable: a nullary atom with nothing but its principal port. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">ROOT</span></code> | The root of a term — where the answer ends up. A nullary atom, distinguished only by its rules. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">CONST</span></code> | An opaque constant. A nullary atom that `DUP` copies and `ERASE` consumes. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">rules</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RuleBook</span></code> | The rule book for this vocabulary: linear beta reduction, plus recursive `DUP` and `ERASE` against both atoms and structure. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">betaBridgeDemo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span></code> | A minimal APP/LAM bridge demo. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">duplicatedConstantDemo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span></code> | A tiny nonlinear sketch: a single `CONST` is demanded by two roots through a `DUP`, so the rewrite system has to copy it. No `LAM` and no body — `betaBridgeDemo` is the one with those. This is not a full term encoder, but it gives the rewrite system something resource-sensitive to do. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">eraseApplicationDemo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Net</span></code> | Erase an application tree to demonstrate explicit garbage collection. |

## Colormaps.kt { #colormaps-kt }

### Colormaps { #colormaps-kt-colormaps }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Colormaps</span></code>

Perceptually-uniform colormaps as named colour ramps — matplotlib's viridis / magma / plasma / inferno, Google's turbo, Kenneth Moreland's coolwarm diverging map, and a plain grayscale. Each map is a table of evenly-spaced RGB control points taken from the published data (the viridisLite 9-class swatches for the matplotlib family, the turbo_srgb_floats LUT sampled every 16th entry, Moreland's cool→warm table); `sampleStops` interpolates linearly between them. This is reusable domain code — the single source of truth for the `showHeatmap` visualizer and RectSL's `colormap`/`cmap`, `bars`, `heat`, and `scatter` words, and directly callable from Kotlin.

## LazyValueVisualizer.kt { #lazyvaluevisualizer-kt }

The lazy half of value display: rather than inline a large structure, show one summary line plus
links into the server-side browsers.

`LazyValueVisualizer.visualize` — reached in a box as `h2` — passes anything small or
unrecognised straight to `ValueVisualizer`. For maps, lists, arrays and `FloatBuffer` /
`IntBuffer` it instead retains the value under a token and emits a summary, `outliner` and
`columns` links, and an embedded `/h2-explorer` iframe. Those tokens live in an in-memory
retention table (10 minutes, 256 entries), so the links only resolve against the running server
and go stale after that.

The private `Browsable` wrappers behind those routes page rather than copy: children are grouped
into range-labelled directories of at most 96 entries, and a map with more than 20,000 entries is
iterated on demand instead of snapshotted. `registerH2Value` adds a per-type adapter returning an
[`H2ValueSnapshot`](visualization.md#lazyvaluevisualizer-kt-h2valuesnapshot) when a type should be summarised or unwrapped differently, and
`lazyInlineExpanderHtml` is the inline "… +N more" link `ValueVisualizer` emits for elided
content.

## ValueVisualizer.kt { #valuevisualizer-kt }

The default value display for Field output areas: a Kotlin value in, a compact HTML fragment out.

`ValueVisualizer.visualize` is the entry point; `Any.h` and `Box.viz` are how it is usually
reached — `.h` hands back the fragment, `viz` displays it into a channel of a live box. A type
can take over its own rendering either by implementing [`ToHTML`](visualization.md#valuevisualizer-kt-tohtml) or by registering a printer with
`registerValuePrinter`; both are trusted to return well-formed HTML, while ordinary strings,
characters, keys and reflected values are escaped here.

Output is deliberately bounded — [`ValueVisualizer`](visualization.md#valuevisualizer-kt-valuevisualizer)'s own KDoc below covers dispatch order, the
built-in formatters and the size limits. Whatever those limits elide (the tail of a long string
or list, extra fields of an object) becomes an expander link, resolved later by
`renderLazyFragment` from the server's `/lazy-value-fragment` route, so the rest of the value is
only ever rendered if someone asks for it.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/visualization/ValueVisualizer.kt`

**Used in:** [Visualizers, Displays, and Little Instruments](../visualizers.md), [Agent transcript gallery](../agent_transcripts.md)

## plotly.kt { #plotly-kt }

Plotly helpers — the short way to get a chart out of a box, wrapping `space.kscience.plotly`.

`linePlot`, `scatter`, `scatterSized` and `violin` cover the common shapes (lists of numbers,
`Vec2`, `Vec3`) and hand back a `Plot` already run through `darkMode`, the repo dark theme with
data-first margins. `showSignals` goes one step further: pass `"label" to values` pairs and it
traces them against a shared x with the `signalPalette`, optionally min-max normalized and with
dashed reference marks, then displays the plot into a channel of a live `Box` — it is already on
screen when it returns, so do not display it again.

`toHtml` renders a `Plot` into an HTML fragment via [`PlotlyIntegration`](visualization.md#plotly-kt-plotlyintegration). That fragment calls
`Plotly.react` in the browser, so the page has to have the Plotly library loaded already;
without it the fragment logs to the console and draws nothing.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/visualization/plotly.kt`

**Used in:** [Values over time: interpolants & keyframes](../interpolants_examples.md)

## tables.kt { #tables-kt }

Tabular output — the structure, and the one renderer for it.

[`Table`](visualization.md#tables-kt-table) is the counterpart of `showSignals` for data that is rows and columns rather than a
signal: build it, hand it to `Box.showTable` (or just let a box's last expression be one), and it
arrives on screen in the repo's output style. It implements [`ToHTML`](visualization.md#valuevisualizer-kt-tohtml), so `ValueVisualizer`
dispatches it ahead of everything else — `display(channel, table)`, `table.h`, and a returned
`Table` all render through `Table.toHTML` with no extra wiring.

Why this exists: a box that wants a table has, until now, hand-rolled
`<table style='border-collapse:collapse…'>` with its own font stack, paddings and greys. A dozen
files under `src/` do exactly that and no two agree, which is a lot of markup standing between a
reader and what the box is actually saying.

The part that is not just formatting is `Table.expect`. A table in a doc or a live box usually
carries a *claim* — "every builder advanced one frame per pump", "no residual exceeds 1e-6" — and
a reader is otherwise asked to verify it by scanning cells. State the claim and the cells that
break it colour themselves, the footnote says how many did, and `Table.deviations` hands the same
list back to a test. That is the difference between showing a grid and showing an assertion you
can watch fail.

Trust model, same as the rest of value display: text produced by default formatting is escaped;
a string returned from a `Table.format` lambda is trusted HTML and inserted as-is.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/visualization/tables.kt`

**Used in:** [Frames, and what a frame is](../animation_time_model.md), [How the popup decides](../how_the_popup_decides.md), [Keyboard shortcuts, and how to change them](../keybindings.md)

| --- | --- |

| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">TABLE&#95;TEXT</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | Default body text colour, matching `ValueVisualizer`'s wrapper. See `TABLE_MUTED` on the hex. |

### Align { #tables-kt-align }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">Align</span></code>

Horizontal alignment of a [`Table`](visualization.md#tables-kt-table) column. Numeric columns default to `RIGHT`, everything else `LEFT`.

Constants: `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `CENTER`.

### Deviation { #tables-kt-deviation }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Deviation</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">row</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">because</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

One cell that failed a `Table.expect` check: its row index, column name, value, and the reason given.

### CellRole { #tables-kt-cellrole }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CellRole</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cssClass</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>

The semantic colour roles, shared with `markdown()`'s `{role:text}` spans — same six names, same `field-md-*` classes, so the same `--field-*` design token backs both. A cell that means "good" and a markdown span that means "good" are therefore the same colour by construction, and neither spells a hex literal.

Constants: `ACCENT`, `MUTED`, `DIM`, `OK`, `WARN`, `BAD`.

### Table { #tables-kt-table }

<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Table</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">header</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">note</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ToHTML</span></code>

Rows, columns, and the claims made about them.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">title</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Optional line drawn above the table, in the accent colour. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">note</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | Optional footnote spanning every column. Deviation counts are appended to it. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">header</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The column names, in order. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rows</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | The rows appended so far, each padded to `header`'s width. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxRows</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many rows to draw before eliding the tail. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">showHeader</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Whether to draw the header row. A label→value summary built by `facts` has no header worth showing — "key" and "value" over two obvious columns is furniture — so that turns this off. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">row</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">vararg</span> <span class="n">values</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Appends one row. Short rows are padded with `null`; a row wider than `header` is an error. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">row</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">values</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Appends one row from a list. Short rows are padded with `null`; too-wide rows are an error. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">rows</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">values</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Appends many rows. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">align</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">align</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Align</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Overrides the inferred alignment of a column. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">color</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Colours a column's cells. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">accent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">vararg</span> <span class="n">columns</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Colours these columns from `signalPalette`, in order — so a table and a plot of the same quantities agree on which colour means which series. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">role</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">role</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">CellRole</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Gives a column's cells a semantic [`CellRole`](visualization.md#tables-kt-cellrole) instead of a colour. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">roleBy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">role</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">CellRole</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Gives each cell of a column a [`CellRole`](visualization.md#tables-kt-cellrole) chosen from its value — the per-*cell* counterpart of `color`, for a column that means something different row by row (ran / did not run, converged / diverged). Return null to leave a cell alone. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">bar</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">max</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">120</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Draws a numeric column's cells as proportional bars *as well as* text — the shape a ranked score wants: top-k labels, vote tallies, per-stage timings. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">format</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">format</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | Formats a column's cells. The returned string is **trusted HTML** and is not escaped, which is how a cell gets a link, a unit, or a nested fragment; escape it yourself if it came from outside. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">expect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">because</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ok</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | States a claim about one column: cells for which `ok` is false take `CellRole.BAD`, gain a tooltip, are counted in the footnote, and appear in `deviations`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">expect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">because</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">ok</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="n">row</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">column</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Any</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Table</span></code> | States a claim about every cell, given its row index, column name and value. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">deviations</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Deviation</span><span class="p">&gt;</span></code> | Every cell that failed an `expect` check — the same list the rendering colours, so a test can assert on the claim the figure makes rather than on its markup. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toText</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A plain-text rendering, for a terminal, a log, or a test's failure message. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toHTML</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | The rendered table — dispatched by `ValueVisualizer` for `display`, `.h` and box return values. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">toString</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span></code> | A shape summary; `toText` is the one that prints the contents. |

</div>
